newsitem.title: INDIA: India leader loses bail in corruption scandal case.
newsitem.headline: India leader loses bail in corruption scandal case.

text.p: An Indian court on Thursday denied a request by a powerful politician for legal protection against arrest in a $280 million corruption scandal case that has rattled the ruling centre-left coalition.
A judge in Patna rejected the application by Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, in the case, which involves the alleged siphoning of animal welfare funds in Bihar.

"The application for anticipatory bail is rejected," Judge Daljit Singh Dhaliwal told a crowded courtroom in an order that sent the New Delhi stock market's benchmark index down 17.43 points to 883.10 within minutes. It closed at 884.31.
The premier Bombay stock index fell 24.56 points to a close of 4,226.57 ahead of the ruling.

Yadav says he is innocent and will not resign from his post. His lawyer was quoted by the Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying that Yadav would appeal to the Supreme Court against the rejection of the bail, allowed under Indian law to people who wish to avoid possible arrest.
The rejection of the bail came minutes before parliament began a scheduled discussion on the scandal, which caused an uproar in both houses on Wednesday and Thursday.

Yadav's refusal to resign has provoked a national debate on corruption and posed a political challenge to Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition which is under political pressure but no legal obligation to oust him.
The 15-party alliance is currently debating whether or not to admit a faction he formed earlier this month after breaking off from Gujral's Janata Dal over differences linked to party elections.
"As a result of the court judgement, a new situation has arisen," Gujral told parliament at the start of the debate.

"Both in private and public I have advised the chief minister of Bihar to step down but he did not," he said. "I want to assert not my authority, but the legality or the majesty of the rule of the law."

Gujral's coalition is facing a dilemma in dealing with Yadav's Rashtiya Janata Dal (RJD) because he is a powerful low-caste leader with mass support in his state but is seen hurting the alliance's image nationally.
The prime minister's party colleagues, coalition partners and legislators of the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have been leading protests against Yadav.
"The main point basically is that from the first day I have been saying that anybody who...wants to work in public life should keep himself above suspicion," Gujral said.
The judge said it was not proper for the accused to be granted bail in the case, involving alleged irregularities spread over 10 years.

"This is not only a fraud against the people but a crime against the nation too," Judge Dhaliwal said of the scandal, in which investigators have named 56 politicians and officials for the alleged use of fictitious firms to milk state funds.
"Such a huge withdrawal of money from the government treasuries over the years could not be possible without the knowledge of the politicians," he said.

The scandal led to unruly behaviour that forced the adjournment of the upper house of parliament, the Rajya Sabha, on Wednesday, the opening day of the annual monsoon session. The lower house, the Lok Sabha, also witnessed an opposition uproar over the issue.
